line: ASUS ROG Flow Z13 (2025, GZ302) gaming tablet
config_name: ROG Flow Z13 (2025) — Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16C/32T) / Radeon 8060S iGPU, 32GB LPDDR5x-8000 unified, 1TB SSD, 13.4" QHD+ 180Hz touch (GZ302EA-XS96)

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 'Strix Halo' (16-core Zen 5, 32 threads, up to 5.1GHz, 80MB cache)
specs.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S integrated (40 CU RDNA 3.5, shares unified memory)
specs.ram_type: LPDDR5x-8000 quad-channel unified, soldered (up to 24GB allocable as VRAM)
specs.display_type: ROG Nebula IPS, glossy touch, 100% DCI-P3, Dolby Vision, Adaptive-Sync, Gorilla Glass 5, flicker-free (no PWM)
specs.ports: 2x USB-C USB4 (DP1.4 + PD), 1x USB-A, HDMI 2.1, microSD, 3.5mm combo
specs.webcam: 1440p front with Windows Hello face recognition + rear 4K camera
specs.speakers: 2 stereo speakers + dual smart amps (described as weak by Notebookcheck)
specs.keyboard_notes: detachable ROG keyboard cover with folding stand; larger keycaps and much bigger touchpad than 2023 model; RTINGS calls the feel 'mushy' on an incline
specs.pen_support: ASUS Pen 2.0 (MPP 2.6) supported, sold separately; 10-point touch

battery.notes: 70Wh. Notebookcheck measured 9h20 Wi-Fi browsing @150 nits/60Hz and 7h30 @180Hz; 6h18/5h43 at max brightness; H.264 video 12h44; only 0h51 under max load at max brightness. Owners report roughly half the 60Hz figure in mixed real use with 180Hz and GPU boost enabled (see SHARED-flow-z13.md calibration).

price.notes: Verified on bestbuy.ca 2026-11-24: $2,699.99 with 'SAVE $400' badge, 'Selling Fast', Sold and shipped by Best Buy, model GZ302EA-XS96, web code 20122746, BBY rating 4.7/5 (67 reviews). Open-box units from $2,304.99. EU launch RRP was 2,499 EUR for this spec.

offers.name: ASUS ROG Flow Z13 13.4" Touchscreen Gaming Laptop - AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 - 32GB RAM - 1TB SSD - AMD Radeon 8060S - Off Black

reviews.quote: The Ryzen AI Max+ 395 offers enormous amounts of CPU performance in multi-core scenarios thanks to 16 Zen 5 cores, which rivals the Ryzen 9 7945HX3D. This is impressive for a 13-inch device... The integrated graphics card Radeon 8060S is by far the fastest x86 iGPU and is neck-and-neck with the GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop (with a TGP range between 65-75 Watts) in games.

Its performance is impressive for a tablet with integrated graphics, but it falls short compared to gaming laptops with discrete graphics cards. This is a unique device that's difficult to position in the broader market, as there are no other gaming-focused tablet PCs from other brands.
The AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" inside the Z13, with the latest Ryzen 8060S GPU built into it, is not just capable—it's a step up from most of the gaming laptops out there.
The calling card of the new Flow Z13 is the processor: AMD's Ryzen AI Max, which reinvents the tablet's capabilities without adding a separate graphics chip.

praises: Strix Halo CPU punch in a 1.6kg 13-inch tablet — r/FlowZ13: 'It's compact, very powerful, battery life is decent, and it should accelerate common architecture apps like Creo and Revit'
The 8060S iGPU genuinely plays modern AAA at 1080p/1440p with FSR — owners call it 'truly an all in one that performs at a high level. It's awesome.'
Noise levels lower than expected for the power: 'Burst performance is really good and noise levels are low due to good thermal design' (r/FlowZ13 experiences thread)
180Hz flicker-free 100% DCI-P3 touchscreen with pen support — RTINGS notes the panel is 'entirely flicker-free' unlike OLED rivals, and touch/pen make it far more versatile than a clamshell
Real ports without dongles (dual USB4, HDMI 2.1, USB-A, microSD) plus a user-replaceable M.2 2230 SSD — the one thing that IS upgradeable
complaints: Battery under load is poor: 0h51 max-brightness/max-load on Notebookcheck's 70Wh cell, and owners report roughly half the 9h20 light-use figure once 180Hz and GPU boost are on
Fan behaviour: recurring r/FlowZ13 threads ('New Z13 owner, crazy fan noise and power draw', 'the fan is almost always [on]') about spin-up on light loads; NBC measured 45.4 dB(A) under load
Coil whine reports (r/FlowZ13 'High Pitch noise - something to worry about?', Level1Techs 'Asus Flow Z13 - Coil Whine?')

32GB soldered unified memory is not upgradeable and up to 24GB gets carved out for VRAM, so heavy CPU+GPU multitasking gets tight; NBC lists 'RAM not upgradeable' and 'hardly any maintenance options' (repairability sub-score 40%)

Keyboard cover typing feels 'mushy' on an incline and the tablet is 'rather unstable when using it on a lap' (RTINGS); weak speakers also called out by NBC; no built-in kickstand — the cover is the only stand

design_philosophy: ASUS's bet that a gaming tablet can replace both a gaming laptop and a Surface Pro: the 2025 GZ302 drops the discrete NVIDIA GPU of the 2023 model entirely and bets on AMD's Strix Halo APU, whose 16 Zen 5 cores and 40-CU RDNA 3.5 graphics share one unified LPDDR5x pool. This 32GB/1TB SKU is the volume CA config at Best Buy — enough unified memory to hand ~24GB to the GPU for modern titles while keeping the CPU side comfortable. The trade is a fixed memory ceiling (no upgrade path) and a 14.9mm fan-cooled chassis that must dissipate its full package power behind the display.
rating_notes: Anchor config = the exact 32GB class unit Notebookcheck tested (GZ302EA-RU073W, 32GB/512GB; CA SKU is 1TB) and closest CA match to RTINGS' tested 64GB unit. avg_score 8.7 = Notebookcheck 86.8% normalised to a 10-scale; RTINGS, Ars and PCMag gave verbal-only verdicts and their numeric scores could not be retrieved (RTINGS values are membership-locked) — honest nulls, not invented. Battery rated a tier below NBC's 86% Battery sub-score per SHARED-flow-z13.md calibration (real mixed use ≈ half the 60Hz lab figure). thermals_noise penalised for user-reported fan spin-up on light loads and coil whine beyond what NBC's 83% Noise score implies. keyboard_trackpad rated on the bundled keyboard cover per schema tablet rule (NBC Keyboard 81%/Pointing 93%, RTINGS 'mushy'). ai_ml 7.5: 50 TOPS NPU Copilot+ plus up to 24GB allocable VRAM for local LLMs, but no CUDA. webcam_speakers penalised by NBC's 'weak speakers' con despite good 1440p + 4K cameras. Image URL is a best-guess Best Buy CDN pattern; site has a fallback.
